script: Starfish can clone themselves from just one arm. If a predator bites one off, it isn't just a lost limb. title: Coral Reefs Are Actually Massive Underwater Skeletons
script: Coral reefs are built from millions of tiny animal skeletons. You might think these reefs are just colorful rocks or plants, but they are living colonies. Each tiny creature, called a polyp, secretes a hard limestone shell around its body. Over thousands of years, these layers stack up to form the massive structures we see today. It is basically a giant, underwater skeleton city that protects the whole ocean ecosystem. Would you ever want to go scuba diving through a giant skeleton?

title: The Blue Whale Is Huge But Cannot Swallow A Basketball
script: The largest animal ever can't swallow a basketball. Blue whales grow longer than three school buses, but their throat is only about the size of a grapefruit. When they hunt, they open their gigantic mouths and scoop up thousands of gallons of water full of tiny krill. Then, they push all that water out through huge bristles while keeping the tiny shrimp inside. Isn't it wild that the biggest creature on Earth eats the smallest meals?

claims.note: Seahorses lack teeth in their jaws; they use a tubular snout to suction prey.

claims.claim: Seahorses have no stomach.
claims.note: Seahorses lack a true stomach; their digestive tract is a simple tube where food passes directly to the intestine.

claims.claim: They process food rapidly.

claims.claim: Many species must eat almost constantly to maintain energy.

title: The Veined Octopus Carries Its Own Shelter
script: How an octopus carries its own mobile home. Finding safety on the open seafloor is hard for many soft-bodied creatures. This veined octopus finds discarded coconut shells and stacks them up. It walks across the sand while holding two halves of a shell under its body. When it needs to hide, it pulls the pieces together to build a portable shelter. It is a smart way to stay safe while moving. Would you feel safer if your house could walk with you?

title: How Do Clownfish Change Sex?
script: Most clownfish are born with both male and female reproductive organs. How do they become female? In many species, clownfish live in groups structured by size. The largest fish in the group is typically female, while others remain male. If the female dies, the largest male can undergo a permanent sex change. Nature has wild ways of keeping balance. Would you ever guess a fish could switch like that?

title: The Stingray's Tooth-Like Skin
script: A stingray's skin is covered in tiny, hard scales. These are called dermal denticles, which are unique structures. Denticles share some chemical composition with human teeth. Both are composed of hard, mineralized dental tissue. This armor may help some species reduce drag while swimming. Would you want armor made of dental tissue if you lived in the ocean?

claims.claim: A stingray's skin is covered in tiny, hard scales called dermal denticles.
claims.note: Stingrays are elasmobranchs; their skin is covered in placoid scales known as dermal denticles.

claims.claim: Denticles share some chemical composition with human teeth.
claims.note: Both consist of a pulp cavity, dentin, and an outer layer of enamel-like material (vitrodentine in sharks/rays).

claims.claim: Both are composed of hard, mineralized dental tissue.
claims.note: Both are derived from the neural crest and consist of hydroxyapatite.

claims.claim: This armor may help some species reduce drag while swimming.
claims.note: Research suggests the riblet structure of denticles reduces hydrodynamic drag and turbulence.
